steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Spread pecans onto a baking sheet; toast in the preheated oven until they start to turn golden brown and become fragrant, about 15 minutes. Watch carefully as they bake, they burn quickly. Set aside to cool to room temperature.

Pulse brown sugar, butter, and vanilla together in a food processor several times to thoroughly combine. Butter will be slightly fluffy. Sprinkle in cooled nuts and pulse several times to combine. For more finely ground pecans, pulse several more times. Serve immediately, or pack into a jar with a lid and refrigerate.

raw_recipe.headline: Toasted Pecan Butter
raw_recipe.description: This pecan butter recipe gives a toasty flavor to a fluffy, sweet butter perfect for french toast, pancakes, waffles, biscuits, and other yummy treats.
raw_recipe.name: Toasted Pecan Butter

review.reviewBody: Really good! We'll be making this again for an upcoming family breakfast -- it would top pancakes or any breakfast breads beautifully.

I love it. It has become a staple in our fridge. I like to put a spoonful into my oatmeal in the morning with some toasted pecans. Its wonderful! I ran out of vanilla and used vanilla bean paste one time. Still pretty good, but the original is a hit and I dont like to deviate on this one unless it's out of necessity. Delicious and versatile.

I made this for a family reunion and it was an incredible hit! I used pecan baking pieces which are already chopped very small to save a step in chopping the nuts. I also only used a hand mixer and it worked fine. Excellent quality vanilla does make a difference.
Delicious recipe - didn't use a food processor and it turned out really good as well!

This might be one of the tastiest things I have made. I made it out of homemade butter as a part of a "compound butter flight" that I'm making as a Christmas gift and this is hands down my favorite so far. It tastes like cookie dough. I'm glad it made so much so I can freeze some for our family to have on pancakes Christmas morning. So, so good.

Fantastic! I had fresh pecans from home in Ga, really good. Only thing I did different is I sprinkled the pecans with cinnamon before roasting- awesome. Adds just a small flavor... Will make for friends!

While having breakfast at The Wave restaurant in WDW a couple months ago, I tried Butter Pecan Butter. It was so good I tried finding a recipe for it online when I got home. I came across this recipe. It tastes just like I remember from The Wave! It is delicious on biscuits and I can't wait to try it on pancakes and waffles. I let my mom and sister tr
Great! Skip the sugar and vanilla and just use maple syrup. Really delicious and the maple syrup makes it silky and not grainy.

I MADE THIS FOR CHRISTMAS DAY AND IT WAS A GREAT BIG HIT!!!!!
IT WENT SO NICE WITH OUR HAM DINNER!!
THE ONLY THING I ADDED WAS A TINY SPRINKLE OF CINNAMON!!! PERFECT!!!
I used this on steamed carrots with great results. I've also had it on sweet potatoes.

Served this today on waffles, and it was a nice change from regular butter/margarine. I used ICBINB spread, and the only thing that I wasn't crazy about was the grainy texture from the brown sugar. I'm used to making fruit butters or adding honey, cinnamon or extracts where the texture is always smooth. The graininess didn't kill it for me, it was just different, and the butter-pecan flavor definitely came through nicely. Don't skip toasting the nuts, as it really enhances the pecan flavor in this butter. Thanks Carrie Mae for this new variation on a flavored butter.

I made 1/2 recipe to try this out. I didn't toast the pecans, because nuts usually come roasted anymore. And, I don't like the bitter or slightly burnt taste they get when toasted further. I used a hand emulsion blender for easier clean-up, and chopped the nuts by hand to a ground consistency. I wasn't able to get a strong "butter pecan" flavor. It wasn't bad, it just didn't taste like much more than the ingredients were butter and brown sugar with some ground nuts. Maybe, a drop of butter pecan flavoring may have given it that butter pecan flavor that I was expecting, not sure? This might be good on some pancakes as a change to regular butter, though, with some pancake syrup.
